narrative:
The model determined that you have a 38% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the loan amount you requested, the length of time you wanted to repay it, and the status of your checking account. Surprisingly, both the amount and the duration actually worked in your favor. You asked for 2,579 DM for 12 months, both noticeably lower than the averages among people who were approved. These shorter, smaller requests made the model view you as less risky in those respects.

Unfortunately, the status of your checking account pushed strongly in the opposite direction. Your account is currently in the red (below zero DM), a situation that is relatively uncommon among approved applicants. This single factor was enough to outweigh the positive signals from the smaller loan size and shorter term, tipping the overall prediction toward bad credit risk.

The bank therefore could not approve the loan. To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account balance back into positive territory and maintaining it there for several months before re-applying. This is the clearest lever you have to change how a similar model would evaluate you in the future.
